Document history

Source: R/history.R
history.Rd

A document keeps its full editing history, so earlier versions can be inspected, compared, and restored.

  • doc_frontiers() returns the version the document is currently showing. Unlike the version vector from doc_version(), which is meant for synchronization, frontiers are a compact name for one point in history.

  • doc_frontiers_to_version() and doc_version_to_frontiers() convert between the two kinds of version. For example, converting a row of doc_changes() to a version vector lets doc_export_updates() produce the updates made since that change.

  • doc_compare_frontiers() orders two versions: -1 if x is an ancestor of y, 1 if it is a descendant, 0 if they are the same, and NA if they are concurrent (neither contains the other).

  • doc_changes() returns one row per change in the history, and doc_change() the one change containing a given operation.

  • doc_change_count() and doc_op_count() return the number of changes and of individual operations in the history.

  • doc_changed_containers() returns the ids of the containers modified by the given changes.

  • doc_checkout() moves the document to an earlier version, or back to the latest when frontiers is NULL. While checked out at an earlier version the document is detached: it is read-only, and imported updates are stored but not shown until it returns to the latest version. doc_is_detached() reports this state.

  • doc_detach() detaches the document at its current version, freezing what it shows while imports continue to be stored.

  • doc_set_detached_editing() allows a detached document to be edited, which starts a new branch of history from the checked-out version; doc_is_detached_editing() reports the setting. See the Detached editing section.

  • doc_revert_to() adds new changes that restore the contents of an earlier version and commits them. History is kept, and the revert synchronizes to other replicas like any other edit.

  • doc_diff() returns the differences between two versions.

  • doc_apply_diff() takes the changes that source made between two of its versions and applies them to doc as new, committed edits. With source left as doc this replays or (with the versions swapped) undoes a span of its own history; with another document it copies a span of work across without merging the two histories. The changes are applied by position, so doc must hold contents that match what source held at from; otherwise the call fails or lands edits in the wrong place.

  • doc_record_timestamps() turns on recording of the wall-clock time of each new change. It is off by default.

Usage

doc_frontiers(doc)

doc_changes(doc)

doc_change(doc, peer, counter)

doc_change_count(doc)

doc_op_count(doc)

doc_changed_containers(doc, changes)

doc_frontiers_to_version(doc, frontiers)

doc_version_to_frontiers(doc, version)

doc_compare_frontiers(doc, x, y)

doc_checkout(doc, frontiers = NULL)

doc_is_detached(doc)

doc_detach(doc)

doc_set_detached_editing(doc, enable = TRUE)

doc_is_detached_editing(doc)

doc_revert_to(doc, frontiers)

doc_diff(doc, from, to)

doc_apply_diff(doc, from, to, source = doc)

doc_record_timestamps(doc, record = TRUE)

Arguments

doc

A loro_doc.

peer, counter

The id of an operation: a peer id string and an operation counter.

changes

A data frame of changes, such as rows of doc_changes().

frontiers, from, to, x, y

A version: frontiers from doc_frontiers() (see as_frontiers()), or the version after one change, named by its number in doc_changes() order or by its commit message. For doc_apply_diff(), change numbers and messages refer to source.

version

A version vector from doc_version().

enable

Whether to allow editing while detached.

source

The loro_doc whose history from and to refer to.

record

Whether to record timestamps.

Value

doc_detach() and doc_set_detached_editing() return doc invisibly, and doc_is_detached_editing() a logical. doc_frontiers(), doc_frontiers_to_version(), and doc_version_to_frontiers() return raw vectors. doc_compare_frontiers() returns an integer, doc_change_count() and doc_op_count() integers, and doc_changed_containers() a character vector. doc_changes() and doc_change() return a tibble, doc_is_detached() a logical, and doc_diff() a named list. doc_checkout(), doc_revert_to(), doc_apply_diff(), and doc_record_timestamps() return doc invisibly.

Detached editing

With detached editing enabled, edits made while checked out at an earlier version are recorded as changes that follow that version, concurrent with everything that came after it. Returning to the latest version with doc_checkout(doc) merges the branch with the rest of the history, as if another replica had made those edits.

To keep the branches distinct, the document takes a new random peer id at each checkout while this is enabled, and keeps the last one after returning to the latest version, so do not rely on doc_peer_id() staying fixed. The setting belongs to this loro_doc object and is not saved in exports.

Changes

doc_changes() returns a tibble, in causal order, with columns:

  • peer, counter: the id of the change's first operation.

  • lamport: its logical timestamp.

  • length: the number of operations in the change.

  • timestamp: when it was committed (NA if not recorded).

  • message: the commit message (NA if none).

  • frontiers: a list column holding the version just after the change, suitable for doc_checkout(), doc_revert_to(), doc_diff(), and doc_fork().

Consecutive commits by one peer that carry the same message, or no message, may be stored as a single change, so rows do not correspond one-to-one with calls to doc_commit(). An empty message is the same as no message, and a commit with nothing to commit is dropped along with its message.

Diffs

doc_diff() returns a named list with one element per changed container, named by container id (see container_id()). Each element has a type and:

  • for text, delta: delta ops as in text_apply_delta();

  • for a list or movable list (both have type "list"), delta: ops with retain or delete counts, or insert holding a list of new elements;

  • for a map, updated: a named list of the new values of keys that were set, and deleted: a character vector of keys that were removed;

  • for a counter, increment: the net amount added;

  • for a tree, diff: a list of node changes, each with node, an action ("create", "move", or "delete"), and the parent and 1-based index it now has and, for moves and deletes, the old_parent and old_index it had (NA parents are the top level).

Child containers appear by their contents.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
text = doc_text(doc)

text_insert(text, 1, "Hello")
doc_commit(doc, "greeting")
v1 = doc_frontiers(doc)

text_insert(text, 6, " world")
doc_commit(doc, "audience")
v2 = doc_frontiers(doc)

doc_changes(doc)[, c("lamport", "length", "message")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   lamport length message 
#>     <int>  <int> <chr>   
#> 1       0      5 greeting
#> 2       5      6 audience
str(doc_diff(doc, v1, v2))
#> List of 1
#>  $ cid:root-text:Text:List of 2
#>   ..$ type : chr "text"
#>   ..$ delta:List of 2
#>   .. ..$ :List of 1
#>   .. .. ..$ retain: int 5
#>   .. ..$ :List of 1
#>   .. .. ..$ insert: chr " world"

doc_checkout(doc, v1)
text_get(text)
#> [1] "Hello"
doc_checkout(doc)

doc_revert_to(doc, v1)
text_get(text)
#> [1] "Hello"
